question: The average weight of Ketan, Tushar and Salil is 46 kg. If the average weight of Ketan and Tushar is 36 kg and that of Tushar and Salil is 44 kg, then the weight of Tushar (in kg) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of **Tushar** = [Sum of (**Ketan** + **Tushar**)] + [Sum of (**Tushar** + **Salil**)] − [Sum of (**Ketan** + **Tushar** + **Salil**)]

Weight of **Tushar** = (36 × 2) + (44 × 2) − (46 × 3)

Weight of **Tushar** = 72 + 88 − 138

Weight of **Tushar** = 160 − 138 = 22 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 22 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of **Ketan**, **Tushar**, and **Salil** = 46 kg

Average weight of **Ketan** and **Tushar** = 36 kg

Average weight of **Tushar** and **Salil** = 44 kg

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ea2b202894ea24dd1d11a87778eea93b312783c7d13c50afc7568c27e60e988.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of (**Ketan** + **Tushar** + **Salil**) = 46 × 3 = 138 kg --- (1)

⇒ Total weight of (**Ketan** + **Tushar**) = 36 × 2 = 72 kg --- (2)

⇒ Total weight of (**Tushar** + **Salil**) = 44 × 2 = 88 kg --- (3)

⇒ From equation (1) and (2), Weight of **Salil** = 138 − 72 = 66 kg

⇒ Substitute weight of **Salil** in equation (3):

⇒ Weight of **Tushar** + 66 = 88

⇒ Weight of **Tushar** = 88 − 66 = 22 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 22 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Overlap in Averages

When one entity is included in two different groups, its value can be found by: (Sum of Group 1 + Sum of Group 2) − Total Sum of all unique entities.

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups with n₁ and n₂ elements is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from the **Arithmetic Mean** is always zero.</p
